articles.headline: Sources: Jets RB Breece Hall week-to-week with quad injury
articles.description: Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
New York Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Hall's MRI showed Hall's injury isn't as significant as feared, the sources said.

The Jets said Hall had a thigh injury on Sunday when he was ruled out. Early in the fourth quarter Sunday, Hall was tackled out of bounds and, rolling over his pain, clutched his right thigh.

Hall rushed for 32 yards on 13 carries Sunday and also had three catches for 23 yards before his injury. So far this season he has rushed for 163 yards and has 102 receiving yards in three games. He also has a rushing touchdown.

Hall, in his fifth season with the Jets, signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract extension with the team in the offseason after New York first used the franchise tag to keep him from unrestricted free agency.

articles.headlineJa: NBAレギュラーシーズンの話題：トレード、ニュース、最新情報
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日のメディアデーからの情報を含む、NBA全般の契約、トレード、最新の噂をお届けします。
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 28

Langdon hasn't spoken with Duren all summer ahead of big decision

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren would hold veto power on any trade this season and is an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent, is key.

There are eight projected teams who have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at Media Day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during the Pistons' Media Day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cleveland made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers Media Day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks and then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition, acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multi-team trade and then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible while Harden opted out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves

articles.headline: Clippers' Brandon Ingram to miss start of season after surgery
articles.description: Brandon Ingram, a key part of the Clippers' return in their trade of Kawhi Leonard, will not be available to start the 2026-27 season as he recovers from a surgery that addressed a right heel injury and partially torn Achilles tendon.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Clippers forward Brandon Ingram will not be available to start the 2026-27 season as he recovers from a surgery that addressed a right heel injury and partially torn Achilles tendon.

Interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden said at Clippers media day Monday that doctors discovered and addressed the previously undisclosed Achilles injury while Ingram underwent surgery on his heel in May.

Ingram, 29, has no timetable for a return to the court, but Redden noted that the recovery time for a partially torn Achilles tendon is typically "about six months less" than for a fully torn Achilles. Ingram missed the final two games of the Raptors' first-round series loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers due to the heel injury before undergoing surgery.

The Clippers acquired Ingram and guard Gradey Dick from the Toronto Raptors in a trade for Kawhi Leonard earlier this month.

"It wasn't until we got our hands on [Ingram] here that we started to see where he was at with his progression," Redden said. "He won't be ready for the start of the season, and we'll reevaluate when we get there."

Redden also said guard Bradley Beal is dealing with right knee inflammation after undergoing surgery on his left hip and won't be available for the start of training camp.

Ingram, a two-time All-Star, averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists for the Raptors last season. Once he returns to the court, Ingram projects as the leading scoring option for the new-look Clippers.

"Whenever [Ingram] comes back, when he gets out there, I think our pick-and-roll will be the No. 1 thing we go to," Clippers guard Darius Garland said. "I think that can be really nasty.

"He's super crafty. I'm super excited to play with him for sure."

Ingram is on the Clippers' books for $40 million this season and holds a $41.9 million player option for 2027-28.

articles.headline: Jaguars sorting out ball boy spat after Travis Hunter interception
articles.description: Jaguars coach Liam Coen isn't sure if cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the actual ball from his first NFL interception.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen isn't sure if cornerback Travis Hunter ended up with the actual ball from his first NFL interception.

Hunter spun the ball in celebration and danced after picking off a pass from New England's Drake Maye in the end zone late in the second quarter Sunday.

An NFL ball boy picked it up and then refused to give it to Josh Hines-Allen, even screaming, "Hey, you can't touch me!" when the Jaguars pass rusher tried to grab the ball.

NFL players are allowed to keep game balls, although they get charged a hefty price by the league.

Hines-Allen tried to knock this one out of the ball boy's hands before Jacksonville's equipment manager, George Pellicer, stepped between them.

The ball boy again screamed, "Hey, he pushed me. He can't do that!" as Pellicer worked to retrieve the ball.

Video of the interaction went viral hours after the game, which the Jaguars won 35-6.

"I was just talking about it," Coen said during a Zoom call with reporters Monday. "I haven't gotten a clean answer. We've been in communication with those guys over there. I think they've gotten it sorted out; I can't say for certain if we got the actual ball or not.

"I know there was something that went on there. I think it's all squared away. We'll get it taken care of."

Hunter, the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner and second overall draft pick from Colorado, made a leaping catch on the pass intended for Patriots receiver Efton Chism III. The play prevented New England from cutting into a 14-3 lead just before the break.

"The coach did a great job scheming it up for us," Hunter said after the game. "He called the perfect call for us. We all talked and we communicated on my side of the ball, and I just made it happen."

articles.headline: NFL asks DHS to take down Brian Dawkins social media video
articles.description: The NFL asked DHS to remove a social media post likening former Eagles star Brian Dawkins' greatest hits to immigration agents' treatment of migrants.
articles.body:
The NFL asked the Department of Homeland Security to remove a social media post likening former Philadelphia Eagles star Brian Dawkins' greatest hits to immigration agents' treatment of migrants.

DHS published the X post in question Sunday evening in response to another account's report that a "huge migrant caravan" was approaching the United States' southern border.

"Our time has come," the agency wrote, adding a video of Dawkins' most violent on-field collisions.

Dawkins, in a text, told ESPN he had not given the agency his blessing to post the video but declined to comment further.

"I have very respectfully not given permission," the Hall of Fame safety wrote.

The NFL said it requested the video's removal, though it remained up as of noon ET Monday.

In March, the White House posted video interspersing NFL and NCAA football highlight hits with video of airstrikes on Iranian targets, days after U.S. forces destroyed an elementary school in southern Iran, killing more than 100 children, according to Amnesty International. The NFL declined to say whether it had requested the removal of that video.

That video also remains on the social media site.

Dawkins, one of the most physical defensive backs of his era, retired in 2012 and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2018.

articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns said he wants to get a contract extension done with the Knicks as he has one year and a player option left on his current deal.
articles.body:
TARRYTOWN, N.Y. -- Karl-Anthony Towns reiterated his desire to get a contract extension done while acknowledging the potential discomfort an unsettled situation could bring as the New York Knicks look to defend their NBA title.

"I've made it known I want to play here," Towns said Monday at media day. "I've been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done and step on the floor and feel as comfortable as possible."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million, but it doesn't appear something will get done before the season starts. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York ended a 53-year title drought with a five-game Finals victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

Towns, who turns 31 in November, was asked if he wanted to table contract talks when the season begins so that it wouldn't be a distraction.

"In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had," he said.

Towns' potential extension is at the intersection of the Knicks keeping their championship core together and staying underneath the punitive second apron -- it already cost the team backup center Mitchell Robinson, who signed with the Boston Celtics this summer.

"You ask me to give three facts or two facts about the second apron, I can't do it," Towns said. "I have no interest in that. It is what it is. [Knicks team president] Leon [Rose] trusts me with stuff on the court, and I trust him with that stuff."

But Towns knows these issues can fester through the season. He said he won't ignore them.

"The first thing is we try to talk about everything. We don't leave any elephants in the room," Towns said. "They'll figure it out and our group has done a fantastic job of understanding that we can only control what we can control."

Towns isn't the only starter with a looming contract, as Josh Hart is eligible for an extension. Hart will make $20.9 million this season and there's a team option for $22.3 million in 2027-28.

Hart mentioned the second apron and collective bargaining agreement having played a part in the NBA having eight different champions in eight years, with the Knicks hoping to buck that trend. The challenge could be made tougher in a deeper, top-heavy Eastern Conference and the Knicks' own contractual issues.

"When there's uncertainty, there's gonna be a lot of questions," Hart said. "Rumors and at a human level it can wear people down and it can affect how you handle business on a daily basis. You want to get it done so you don't have to deal with that. At the end of the day, it's a business. For me, as long as I'm wearing this jersey, I'm going to play as hard as I can. Hopefully we can figure that out."

articles.headline: Matthew Stafford makes cameo in Taylor Swift's 'Patient Zero' music video
articles.description: Why, yes, that was Matthew Stafford. Here's why all signs pointed to the reigning NFL MVP's music video cameo.
articles.body:
Never let it be said Matthew Stafford lacks range.

If you find yourself watching Taylor Swift's recently debuted music video for "Patient Zero" and see someone who happens to bear a striking resemblance to the Los Angeles Rams quarterback, that's because it is said quarterback.

In the video, which also stars actors Colin Farrell, Dakota Johnson and Cara Delevingne, the Super Bowl LVI champion and reigning NFL MVP makes a cameo at a black-tie affair alongside his wife, Kelly Stafford. Stafford's not the only athlete in the scene, as former Los Angeles Kings center and two-time Stanley Cup champion Jarret Stoll can be spotted next to him.

For those struck by the randomness of that duo appearing in a Swift video, you clearly don't know the lore.

So let's get into it.

The Staffords are friends with the 14-time Grammy Award winner and her husband, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, as are Stoll and his wife, Erin Andrews. The couples attended the Madison Square Garden wedding of Swift and Kelce this summer alongside Charissa Thompson and her significant other, Steven Cundari -- the latter of whom is also featured in the black-tie event scene of Swift's video posing next to Farrell.

As for Andrews and Thompson, the duo have been vocal supporters of Swift and the Kansas City Chiefs star's relationship since before they started dating, even making a plea on their "Calm Down" podcast for the singer to give Kelce a chance. Meanwhile, the Staffords' four daughters are known Swift fans, with Kelly sharing in 2024 that she and Matthew surprised the girls with a trip to see "The Eras Tour" in New Orleans. Kelly and her daughters also attended the June premiere of "Toy Story 5" in Los Angeles where Swift made a surprise appearance to perform her song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

Then there's the Emmy's Easter egg of it all. Swift sent her fans into overdrive when she appeared via prerecorded video skit at the 87th Emmy Awards alongside her cat, Olivia Benson, and the show's host, Mariska Hargitay, who plays Swift's cat's namesake on "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit." In the sketch, the pop superstar addressed the camera and said, "I think what we're gonna be looking for is hiding in plain sight: Saccharide Aries from the vineyard north or south."

Upon the Stafford reveal, the "Aries" reference has been decoded as a nod to the symbol for the astrological sign for Aries being a ram. As for the rest of the cryptic message? "Saccharide" is a reference to Farrell's role in the show "Sugar," "from the vineyard" is the old French translation of Delevingne and "north or south" is a play on Dakota.

And while you ruminate on all of that, we're going to ponder how we got a Stafford Easter egg before the Tayvis wedding photos. Any day now.
